title: Building my first dirfting game prototype with Astra, Unity and Blender
author: TheNutdev
selftext:
Hey there,

I am building a game prototype where drifting is the core mechanic. I used astra (low to medium effort) with unity and blender to build everything.

I didn’t focus at game looks at any means, thats why you can see those sketchy, low poly models and very basic track. Astra called that game low poly drive, and I think it’s pretty accurate at this state :D

I focused on making the drifting fun and I think it came up pretty well. There was one challenge tho, I wanted to make it feels good on keyboard and it was really hard balancing between real car mechanics and the arcade feeling of such game. However in current state you can initiate and hold drift using known ways like weight shift, e break init, or just wrrum with gas full way down and turning.

Of course it is not close to any decent sim racing game and that’s not the point here. Idk where this small experiment will take me but I have such fun building this little prototype.

I am web dev with 10 years exp if thats interesting for you, and I have to admit that working on game is such refreshing and relaxing. Also astra is so powerful when used well and I cant really express how amazed I feel every time I build/tweak something.

Some technical insight.

From asset side there is not much to talk about if you seen the video, but I just used blender mcp, like everyone else.

I connected my codex (i have 5x pro sub) to unity mcp and thats actually my main tool I use when using unity. Also, notable thing here, when working with web or mobile projects I only use CLI (claude in work, codex in personal projects) but now I tried the gpt app on mac and it is really great so far.

When it comes to building the game first what I did was running a deep research to understand how drift actually works and how to implement it in game. Of course it helped astra a lot to know what we are actually building here and I really recommend you trying this if you haven’t done it before. Then it was pure play testing and giving feedback back and forth. I tried once or twice the feature of codex taking control of my mac and let it play the game and it worked. Thats also why I decided to try the app, as I somehow cannot make it work with cli. However, important note here: AI don’t know what is fun, AI won’t know this, as it doesn’t have a world model, like we do. So to save some tokens and actually have control of whats being created I decide to test myself and just give feedback. I spent few weekly limits building core mechanics and trying different things. What helped me the most was building telemetry and logging system so astra can track whats happening with car during different phases. It was super helpful as I was prompting “hey, car is spinning to fast when entering the corner, check the logs of last run and investigate how to improve”.

Idk if thats worth noting, but I use Polish when talking to astra, as I am not native English I found that using my main language gives me more options to describe the problem correctly.

Also, regarding to some studies Polish is actually really effective when prompting AI. Idk how relevant this study is now so you can correct me. Source: [https://www.euronews.com/next/2025/11/01/polish-to-be-the-most-effective-language-for-prompting-ai-new-study-reveals](https://www.euronews.com/next/2025/11/01/polish-to-be-the-most-effective-language-for-prompting-ai-new-study-reveals)

Thanks for your time reading this. Have a great time building your games folks!
